kevin: Heads-up — after upgrading our workers to redwood-python 1.12.0 we started seeing intermittent 401s for streaming calls and a noticeable billing spike from client retries. Happening in prod, high priority. Repro steps below.

devx: Can you paste the SDK version + a minimal repro?

kevin: Sure. We rolled from 1.11.2 -> 1.12.0. Minimal steps:
```bash
python -m venv v && source v/bin/activate
pip install redwood==1.12.0\``
Code (simplified):
```py
import requests
from redwood import RedwoodClient

s = requests.Session()
s.headers.update({"Authorization": f"Bearer {MY_TOKEN}"})
client = RedwoodClient(session=s)  # used to work on 1.11.x
res = client.stream("generate", {"prompt": "hello"})
for chunk in res:
    print(chunk)
```
Observed: first request to /v1/generate returns 401 on the streaming endpoint, sometimes for the initial polling call. Full worker logs: `HTTP 401 Unauthorized - /v1/generate (Authorization header missing)` 

linda-support: Thanks — sending to eng triage. In the meantime can you confirm `pip show redwood` output and whether you can temporarily pin back to 1.11.2? `pip install redwood==1.11.2` usually fixes compatibility regressions.

kevin: pip show: Name: redwood
Version: 1.12.0
Summary: Redwood inference python client

Tried pinning to 1.11.2 on a canary host and the 401s stop. Confirmed rollout of pin across workers reduces errors and billing.

sam-engineer: Noted. Initial investigation: 1.12.0 changed how internal HTTP sessions are constructed to support connection pooling for async streams. The `session` parameter (requests.Session injection) was refactored; we accidentally broke header propagation when a pre-configured Session with auth headers is passed. Repro unit created. Filing bug INF-4297.

sam-engineer: Quick repro test (run locally):
```py
import requests
from redwood import RedwoodClient, exceptions

s = requests.Session()
s.headers.update({"Authorization": "Bearer BADTOKEN"})
client = RedwoodClient(session=s)
try:
    next(client.stream("generate", {"prompt":"x"}))
except exceptions.HTTPError as e:
    print(e)  # shows 401 and missing auth header on server side
```
This demonstrates the SDK isn't forwarding session headers into the streaming transport.

linda-support: For customers affected, immediate mitigation options: 1) pin to 1.11.2 (`pip install 'redwood==1.11.2'`) 2) export REDWOOD_API_KEY env var on the worker so the client constructs its own auth header instead of relying on injected session 3) if you control each request, pass `api_key=...` to the client constructor rather than relying on a Session.

kevin: We'll roll the pin across the fleet now. Can you give ETA for fix? Billing team is on standby.

sam-engineer: Triage summary: patch to restore session header propagation + add test coverage + explicit deprecation warning will be cut as 1.12.1. Target: hotfix branch today, patch release within 48h if tests pass. INF-4297 assigned to me.

incident-bot: Incident INF-4297 opened by sam-engineer. Priority: P2. Links: internal/issues/INF-4297

devx: Also adding a migration note to the changelog and a snippet showing the recommended pattern using api_key or env var so customers don't hit this after automated upgrades.

kevin: Thanks — pin applied, errors falling back to baseline. Please @sam-engineer paste the exact pip command for customers to use so support can push to them.

linda-support: Command we recc: `pip install 'redwood==1.11.2' --upgrade --force-reinstall` or `pip install 'redwood>=1.12.1,<1.13'` once 1.12.1 ships. I'll add a canned response for support. :white_check_mark:

sam-engineer: Will post the release PR and the 1.12.1 pip URL in this thread when ready. Also logging a follow-up to add a CI test that injects a Session with custom headers.

kevin: Appreciate the fast response team — keeping this thread pinned to the support ticket.

linda-support: Closing loop once 1.12.1 is published and we've notified affected customers.
